title: x402 failure: the signed recipient does not match payTo
summary: The client signed an authorization to an address that is not the payTo in the server requirements, for example because it used stale or altered requirements. Verification fails on the recipient check.

steps.label: Sign to an unexpected address
steps.detail: The requirements the client used named a different payTo than the server expects, for example after a proxy altered the 402 response or a cached copy went stale. The client signed authorization.to for that address.

steps.label: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
steps.detail: The client sends the payload. The accepted field may still echo the server requirements, but the signed authorization names another recipient.

steps.label: POST /verify
steps.detail: The server forwards the payload together with its own copy of the requirements.

steps.label: Return isValid false (recipient mismatch)
steps.detail: The facilitator checks authorization.to against payTo in the server requirements. The spec code is invalid_exact_evm_payload_recipient_mismatch; the TypeScript facilitator reports invalid_exact_evm_recipient_mismatch.

steps.label: 402 with a fresh PAYMENT-REQUIRED
steps.detail: The server refuses the request. The signed authorization still names the other address, so the protection is on the client side: check payTo against what you expect before you sign. The reference server puts the verify reason, invalid_exact_evm_payload_recipient_mismatch, in the error field of the new PAYMENT-REQUIRED.
